source_snapshot.procedure: Send OEM raw `0x30 0x01 <BIOS Major Revision> <BIOS Minor Revision> <BIOS Iteration>` once in-band on localhost and once out-of-band through RMCP+ cipher suite 17, then check response data.
source_snapshot.criteria: Command should be sent without any error.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek recognizes a write but its in-band sample omits `ipmitool`, disables SSH host-key verification, exposes OOB credentials and proposes unrelated `lan print` as readback.

original_test_intent.purpose: Verify that the Wistron OEM command 0x30/0x01 accepts an explicitly supplied three-byte BIOS revision tuple through both local in-band IPMI and remote out-of-band IPMI paths and returns the vendor-defined success response.
original_test_intent.target: The same verified SUT/BMC pair, with one invocation through its host-side system interface and one through the BMC network interface.
original_test_intent.scope: Exactly two path-specific command transmissions using the same approved major/minor/iteration byte tuple. The source does not define BIOS setup-attribute changes, flashing, reboot, persistence testing or generic LAN configuration readback.
original_test_intent.operation: Capture baseline identity/state, validate the OEM command/byte encoding, execute the local `ipmitool raw` command and the remote `ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 ... raw` command separately, preserve raw responses/completion status, and use only the vendor-defined readback if one exists.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: The workbook estimates 15 attended and 15 machine minutes and specifies one in-band and one out-of-band send.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Each path sends the exact tuple without transport or IPMI completion error and returns the response defined by the applicable Wistron OEM command specification. No broader state-change claim is supported without that specification and a defined readback.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: SUT/BMC/BIOS identity; OEM command revision and byte encoding; exact redacted tuple; ipmitool/version; IB and OOB endpoint identity; per-path command, exit/transport/IPMI completion status and raw response; supported readback if defined; before/after BMC/host health and logs.
ambiguities: The title says `Set BIOS Configuration` while the payload fields are BIOS revision bytes; the source does not define the state being written.
The response format, valid byte ranges, idempotency and readback are absent.
It is unclear whether the second send is intended to repeat a state write or merely validate the second transport path.
source_conflicts: The broad title can imply BIOS setup/NVRAM configuration, but the procedure only supplies version components. The vendor OEM definition is required to resolve whether the command updates BMC inventory, BIOS metadata or another state.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly requires the OEM specification, exact bytes, secret-safe transport, approval and supported readback, and rejects `lan print`. It states as fact that the command writes BIOS/NVRAM and can make the SUT unbootable, which is not established by the source and conflicts with revision-byte payload semantics.

applicable_history.decision: V2 replaces the historical PARTIAL label with the formal REQUIRES class and strengthens write safety, but no later user ruling identifies the actual OEM command state or response schema.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Keep the automation class: both transports are automatable after normal vendor/package/approval inputs. Do not label the command a BIOS/NVRAM write or execute it until the Wistron OEM definition resolves the title/payload conflict, state effect, duplicate-send behavior, response and recovery.

available_now: The exact net function, command byte, three payload fields and two required transport contexts are stated.
Read-only SUT/BMC/BIOS identity, BMC reachability, local IPMI interface availability and tool version can be collected before write approval.
missing_inputs: The Wistron OEM owner must supply command 0x30/0x01 request/response schema, valid revision encoding, completion codes, affected state, idempotency/persistence, firmware applicability, readback and recovery.
The testcase owner must resolve whether two writes are required and define the exact approved byte tuple and final acceptance beyond `no error`.
The lab/security owner must provide approved ipmitool builds, protected credentials/endpoints and explicit state-change approval.
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The Wistron BMC/OEM-command owner provides command semantics; the BIOS/test owner provides the intended revision tuple and acceptance; the lab/security owner authorizes the target and protected IB/OOB paths.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Verify the exact SUT/BMC/BIOS identity and firmware compatibility candidate.
Record `ipmitool` versions, local IPMI device availability, protected OOB reachability and baseline health/logs without sending command 0x30/0x01.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not send the OEM command, guess or derive bytes, expose passwords, disable host-key/TLS checks, repeat an unknown-completion write, reboot, clear logs or claim the affected state.
Do not use `ipmitool lan print` as proof of a BIOS revision/configuration update unless the vendor contract explicitly maps it.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: Match the exact firmware to the approved OEM specification, resolve affected state and duplicate-send semantics, validate the tuple and response/readback/rollback, obtain approval, then execute one bounded IB and one bounded OOB operation with independent evidence.

revision_candidate.test_name: Wistron OEM BIOS Revision Tuple Command via In-band and Out-of-band IPMI
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify vendor-defined command 0x30/0x01 with the same approved BIOS major/minor/iteration tuple through the SUT's in-band and BMC's out-of-band IPMI paths, without assuming an undocumented BIOS setup or NVRAM effect.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Only the Wistron server/BMC/BIOS firmware combination explicitly listed by the OEM command specification, using a local system-interface path and a protected RMCP+ remote client.
revision_candidate.target_scope: One verified SUT/BMC pair, one owner-approved three-byte tuple and one separately evidenced invocation per required path. Reboot, flash and BIOS setup validation are outside scope unless the OEM specification explicitly requires them.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Wistron command 0x30/0x01 request/response and firmware matrix; valid byte encoding/ranges; exact approved tuple; affected-state and two-send semantics; supported readback/rollback; approved ipmitool packages; protected endpoints/credentials; write authorization.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: After specification and approval gates close, capture baseline and run `ipmitool raw 0x30 0x01 <major> <minor> <iteration>` locally on the verified SUT. Separately run the source OOB form with RMCP+ cipher suite 17 from the protected client, injecting credentials without command-line disclosure. Record raw response and completion status for each path; perform only the vendor-defined readback and required restoration.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Same-target mapping proven; firmware supported; exact bytes validated; command effect/idempotency known; IB/OOB tools and secrets approved; baseline/readback/recovery available; no concurrent firmware or configuration work.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Identities/versions/timestamp; cited OEM command revision; approved tuple; redacted path and tool evidence; exact per-path command framing; exit, transport and IPMI completion status; complete raw response; supported before/after readback; health/log delta; restoration if required.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The owner-approved Wistron OEM command 0x30/0x01 specification for the target firmware plus the source requirement that both IB and OOB commands complete without error. The specification must define what constitutes a successful response and any state confirmation.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: No execution from the row alone. Do not guess bytes or command effects, expose credentials, disable endpoint validation, broadcast, auto-retry an unknown completion, clear logs, reboot/flash/erase NVRAM or use unrelated LAN output as readback.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Explicit owner approval is required for the exact target, tuple, first send, second-path send and any persistent effect or restoration.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: The agent can collect identity and, after gates close, execute and compare defined responses. The OEM/BIOS owner resolves command semantics, approves duplicate-path behavior and judges platform-specific state/readback.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On target, response or readback mismatch, stop without retry, preserve redacted evidence, determine current state through the vendor-supported independent readback and restore only with the approved procedure. Escalate unknown state to the OEM owner.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Missing/mismatched OEM specification; unresolved title/payload meaning; unsupported firmware; invalid/guessed tuple; wrong target/path; exposed secret; ambiguous completion; first send leaves unknown state; second send not proven safe; missing readback/recovery; or any unapproved reboot/flash/write.

identified_defects: The source title and payload do not establish the same state semantics.
DeepSeek's IB sample omits `ipmitool` and weakens endpoint/credential safety.
DeepSeek's proposed `lan print` readback is unrelated unless the OEM spec says otherwise.
V2 overstates BIOS/NVRAM and unbootable risk without vendor evidence.
reason_for_change: Preserve the exact two-path OEM command while separating known command bytes from unknown affected-state semantics; execution remains gated without inventing a BIOS/NVRAM effect.

new_technical_evidence.title: Source testcase Wistron-BMC-00949-V003
new_technical_evidence.applicability: This exact Wistron OEM command row
new_technical_evidence.supports: The transmitted payload is explicitly BIOS major revision, minor revision and iteration; the row does not state a BIOS setup attribute, flash or NVRAM operation.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: OEM command semantics, response, persistent effect, readback and duplicate-send behavior are private/vendor-specific and unavailable in the source.

removed_ambiguities: Separates command transport validation from an unproven BIOS/NVRAM effect.
Makes first-send unknown completion a stop condition before the second path.
Defines the OEM specification as the only authority for response/readback and recovery.
resolved_blockers: Lack of the vendor specification is treated as a supply/approval readiness gate, not proof that the two paths are permanently non-automatable.
remaining_blockers: The command's actual state effect and valid response are unresolved.
The exact tuple, two-send safety, readback and recovery require owner approval.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 retains V2's secret and write controls but removes unsupported claims of BIOS/NVRAM modification and unbootability, identifies the title/payload conflict and prevents the OOB send after an ambiguous IB result.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The validator recovered the exact two-path purpose, one SUT/BMC and one tuple, all missing OEM inputs, read-only inventory, first-send gate before OOB, evidence, authorization, stops and engineer decisions. It identified the unresolved OEM specification and duplicate-send semantics as PLATFORM_HANDOFF_DEFECT, not a contract defect, and warned that execution despite these gates would be MODEL_PLANNING_ERROR.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: Functionality row 1677 sends 0x30/0x01 with three BIOS revision bytes through one IB and one OOB path.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 adds strong gates but treats an undocumented BIOS/NVRAM effect as established fact.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Allow identity/tool/path inventory only until OEM semantics, exact tuple, response/readback, two-send safety and recovery are approved.
